title: Rapid cross-pool talent swap: contingency protocol and conversion rubric
body:
Purpose:
This is a working protocol for executing short-term cross-pool talent swaps to cover urgent capacity gaps (0–12 weeks) with a low-friction conversion path if the placement proves successful. The doc combines a decision checklist, rapid interview rubric for intake teams, an onboarding micro-checklist, and guidance for conversion from temporary swap -> permanent transfer or backfill hire.

Context & when to use:
- Use when an active hiring pipeline cannot meet a short-term SLA (examples: Dedicated GPU ops surge, critical bug-fix on serving runtime, customer on-call coverage) and the owning team needs immediate skilled capacity.
- Not a substitute for hiring; intended as emergency/accelerative tactic for 2–12 week windows.
- Trigger examples: hiring freeze + critical incident, unexpected attrition within 2 weeks of a launch, key customer support escalations requiring product domain knowledge.

Decision cadence (who signs off):
1) Team lead requests swap and completes Swap Intake Form (link in linked_artifacts).
2) People Ops assesses eligibility and suggests candidate pools.
3) Receiving manager + people partner + originating manager + Eng HR (if >8 weeks) must sign.
4) For swaps >8 weeks or conversion intent, Director-level signoff required.

Eligibility & constraints:
- Candidate eligibility: must be full-time Redwood employee or active contractor eligible for internal mobility (no PIP or active performance plan).
- Minimum notice to originating team: 3 business days unless emergency declared by SRE/Head of Eng.
- Swap load: max 20% of headcount from a single pod concurrently.
- Compensation: baseline unchanged for swaps under 12 weeks; any scope/role change requires comp review.

Swap lifecycle checklist (rapid):
- [ ] Swap Intake Form submitted (link) with problem statement, success criteria, critical dates.
- [ ] People Ops confirms candidate pool availability and flags skills gap.
- [ ] Receiving manager drafts 1-week mission and 4-week measurable outcomes for the swappee.
- [ ] Originating manager documents handoff tasks and critical on-call windows.
- [ ] Security & access pre-check: list of systems needed; pre-approved minimal access pattern for temporary swaps.
- [ ] Manager orientation slot scheduled (30–60m) on day 0; buddy assigned for first 2 weeks.
- [ ] Daily standups for week 1 with originating manager included as needed.
- [ ] Mid-swap 1:1 check at week 2 and week 4 to surface blockers.

Rapid interview / intake rubric (10–20 minute focused assessment)
Purpose: allow receiving teams to quickly evaluate fit for a short-term placement when there is insufficient runway for a full interview loop. Keep it pragmatic and domain-specific.
Scoring: 0–3 scale per dimension (0 = missing/unsafe, 1 = limited, 2 = competent, 3 = strong). Total threshold for go: >=8/12 with no 0s in safety-critical areas.
Dimensions (pick 3–5 for each swap depending on role):
- Domain familiarity (product area, infra stack): 0–3
- Practical debugging / problem triage (example-based question): 0–3
- On-call & incident response experience (procedures, pager calm): 0–3
- Communication & async handoffs (doc + issue description quality): 0–3
- Language/library/infra competency (Python/C++, k8s, CUDA, etc): 0–3
- Security & compliance awareness (if handling PHI/PII or private deployments): 0–3
Instructions for interviewer:
- Keep the session 15 minutes. Start with the one-sentence mission they would take on. Ask 2 focused example questions (one technical, one process). Fill scores in the intake form and record one-line notes (strengths, immediate risks).
- If candidate scores a 0 on "on-call & incident response" but role requires on-call, do not proceed without a short remediation plan (shadowing).

Template example (to copy into form):
Candidate: __________  Role: __________ Duration: __________
List 3 immediate tasks: 1) ______ 2) ______ 3) ______
Scores: Domain __ /3 | Debug __ /3 | On-call __ /3 | Comm __ /3 | Infra __ /3
Quick notes: __________
Decision: Green / Yellow (with shadowing plan) / Red

First-week onboarding micro-checklist (condensed for swaps):
Day 0
- [ ] Access: token, read-only dashboards, repo access scoped to task
- [ ] 30–60m mission kickoff with receiving manager
- [ ] Assign buddy and calendar invites for first week
- [ ] Add to incident rotation read-only materials
Day 1–3
- [ ] Run 1 live incident simulation (walkthrough) with buddy
- [ ] Shadow an on-call rotation (if applicable)
- [ ] Complete a small commit/PR to confirm dev environment chain
End of week 1
- [ ] 1:1 with manager: confirm success metrics and pain points
- [ ] Update handoff doc for originating team

Conversion pathway (temporary -> permanent):
Signals to consider for conversion:
- Consistent performance against 4-week outcomes (>=80% completion),
- Positive peer feedback in 360 check at week 4,
- No critical security/compliance concerns,
- Business case: cost of backfill vs conversion, ramp time saved.
Conversion steps (if pursuing):
- [ ] Receiving manager files Conversion Intent note and business case in linked_artifacts (JIRA:HR-8472).
- [ ] People Ops runs comp alignment and checks manager's matrix for headcount and budget.
- [ ] Originating manager consulted re: permanent change; transfer timeline agreed.
- [ ] Standard hiring loop initiated if needed (can shorten to 1–2 interviews + hiring manager review for internal transfers).

Risk & mitigation notes (common pitfalls):
- Origin team under-resourced after swap: mitigation -> max 2 concurrent swaps from same pod, knowledge transfer checklist required.
- Skill mismatch discovered in week 2: mitigation -> time-boxed shadowing + reduce scope to non-critical tasks.
- Compliance gating (private deployments): mitigation -> pre-approval from security before swap begins; if not approved, swap cannot touch the sensitive systems.

Open questions / TODOs (draft):
- Create a simple payroll/comp guidance doc for swaps >12 weeks where comp uplift may be needed.
- Automate the intake form (people-ops backlog ticket).
- Evaluate metrics to report: swap fill time, conversion rate, originating team sentiment delta. Proposed reporting cadence monthly.

Quick metrics proposal to capture after pilot (first 6 months):
- Swap fill time (hours)
- % swaps converted to permanent
- Originating team satisfaction (Net Promoter style, -100 to +100)
- Mean time to restore originating capacity (days)

Notes to reviewer:
This is intentionally pragmatic/low-bureaucracy to be used in emergencies and short-term surges. Please comment inline in the Confluence doc linked above when you have edits.

Recent changes log:
- 2025-10-12: initial draft (Arielle)
- 2025-11-02: added rapid rubric & scoring (Devon)
- 2026-02-15: tightened conversion approval flow; added Director signoff clause for >8 weeks (María)
